subject: Clarification: EU data residency / region pinning and cross-region processing
messages:
From: Emma Brown <emma.brown@acmehealth.com>
To: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2026-03-11T09:12:00+01:00
Subject: EU residency & DPA questions

Hi Neha,

Thanks for the DPA we received via the procurement portal. Before we move forward I'd like to confirm a few items related to data residency and cross-region processing for Acme Health's PII workload:

- Can Redwood guarantee that all customer request payloads and generated outputs for our environment are stored and processed only in the EU (Frankfurt) region, and not replicated to other regions for inference?
- Are there automatic fallbacks that could route traffic to a non-EU region for availability reasons? If so, what controls/notifications do we get?
- Please provide a list of subprocessors and indicate where (region) they may process data.
- For backups, telemetry, or support access, what is the cross-border transfer policy?

We want to ensure the DPA includes clear region-pinning commitments and scope for cross-border transfers. I can share a redline from our legal team after we get these points clarified.

Best,
Emma
Emma Brown
DPO, Acme Health
emma.brown@acmehealth.com

From: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>

Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, mina_haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: EU residency & DPA questions

Hi Emma — thanks for sending these up-front. Quick answers, and attaching our current DPA (DPA_Redwood_v2026.pdf) for your team to review.

- Region pinning: Yes, we support project-level region pinning. For hosted customers we can pin inference and associated storage to EU (Frankfurt) region. That means request handling, ephemeral inference execution, and persistent outputs (logs/embeddings) are kept in the pinned region by default.

- Failover and fallbacks: We do have configurable availability fallbacks. By default we keep fallbacks within the same geo (EU) and within our EU capacity pool. We can also set a strict contractual requirement to disable cross-region fallback entirely for your project (at the cost of no cross-region HA). Any fallback that would route outside the EU requires explicit customer opt-in.

- Subprocessors: primary subprocessors are the cloud provider (VMs/storage in eu-central-1), the monitoring provider (ObservIQ - EU tenant), and our logging indexer (SearchStream - EU region). A full subprocessors list and region table is in section 5 of the attached DPA.

- Backups/support: Backups are retained in the pinned region for 90 days by default. We do replicate snapshots to a geographically-separated archive for long-term durability in rare cases; that behavior is opt-in and can be disabled. Support access from engineers outside the EU is available only via just-in-time access with logged audit events and customer notifications; we can add stricter clauses to the DPA if required.

Next steps: Mina (legal) will review the DPA redlines your team shares and propose contract language for hard region guarantees. If helpful, we can also schedule a short technical call to walk through how region pinning is configured in the Console.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai

[Attachment: DPA_Redwood_v2026.pdf (pdf)]

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-03-12T10:23:00+01:00
Subject: Redwood DPA — potential redlines for region guarantees

Emma / Neha — following Neha's note I reviewed the DPA and made a few suggested redlines focused on the region-pinning commitments. High level:

- Add a new clause (Section 3.4) that customer data shall be processed and stored only within the customer-selected region(s) unless the customer provides prior written consent.
- Define narrowly the exceptions: (a) emergency support (with customer notification and logged JIT access), (b) explicit archival replication (customer opt-in), and (c) legal compulsion (where we will notify the customer unless prohibited).
- Add an obligation for Redwood to provide a subprocessors geographic table and 30 days' notice before onboarding a subprocessor that would process data outside the pinned region.
- Auditability: monthly attestations for region residency and an on-demand audit right (reasonable scope).

I've attached our redline. If Acme is comfortable with the proposed language, we can incorporate it directly into the DPA and route to procurement. If there are specific technical concerns (e.g., ephemeral cache eviction that could persist in other zones), please highlight them and we can propose controls.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance | Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Redwood DPA — potential redlines for region guarantees

Thanks Mina — helpful. A couple of technical clarifications from our cloud assessment team (cc'd):

- Cache & KV stores: does Redwood ever asynchronously populate cross-region caches or KV replicas that might contain derived embeddings or request metadata? We need to ensure derived artifacts do not leave the EU.
- Model updates: are model re-compilations, quantization jobs, or model-version builds ever executed in non-EU regions? If the model artifact includes customer-provided prompts or telemetry, that could be a data transfer concern.
- Subprocessor details: can you confirm the full set of subprocessors and the region for each? Our procurement wants this as a table in the DPA appendix.

Also, on backups: 90 days in-region retention sounds good — please confirm if encrypted snapshots ever transit to other regions for long-term archive and whether those archives are encrypted with customer-managed keys.

Regards,
Emma Brown
DPO, Acme Health

Emma — thanks for the thorough questions and for looping your cloud assessment partner. Quick summary / commitments from Redwood side:

1) Region pinning: configurable at the project/tenant level in the Console. When pinned to eu-central-1 (Frankfurt) inference execution, ephemeral caches, embeddings storage, and logs are kept in that region. We will add a DPA clause that forbids replication outside the pinned region except for the narrow exceptions Mina outlined.

2) Cross-region caches & KV: our runtime uses local ephemeral caches per region. We do not asynchronously populate cross-region caches with customer-derived embeddings or request payloads. Replication to other regions only occurs if a customer enables cross-region HA or explicitly opts into multi-region deployment.

3) Model builds/updates: model compilation, quantization, and vendor-supplied model updates are normally performed in the same region for hosted deployments. For rare operational reasons (e.g., urgent security patching or capacity shortages) a build may briefly execute in a different region — we will commit to (a) notify the customer in advance when possible, (b) anonymize and strip customer-specific payloads from build inputs, and (c) log all such events. We can also add contractual language to require prior customer approval for any builds that touch customer data across borders.

4) Subprocessors: we'll provide a dated appendix listing each subprocessor, their role, and processing region. We will also give 30 days' notice before adding any subprocessor that would process data outside the pinned region.

5) Backups & encryption: long-term archive replication is opt-in. When enabled, archives are encrypted at rest with provider keys by default; we support customer-managed keys (KMS) for EU-only key material if required.

Next steps:
- Mina will incorporate the agreed language into the DPA and return a consolidated redline.
- Neha will share a short technical runbook and the Region_Pinning_Design.pdf to your cloud team.
- If agreeable, we can sign the DPA and schedule a 30-minute tech walkthrough next week.
